question.text: This Ecumenical Council from 1545 to 1563 was the Catholic Church's response to the Protestant Reformation.
question.clue: This event, which resulted in the production of the Roman Catechism, lasted for twenty-five sessions under Paul III, Julius III, and Pius IV.

swap.leadin: The Lateran Treaty governed the relationship between this country and its much larger neighbor.
swap.text: Name this country, whose flag and coat of arms both depict a pair of crossed keys. Its head of state is elected through a conclave by the College of Cardinals.
swap.answerHtml: Vatican City [or the Vatican City State, or Status Civitatis Vaticanae, or Stato della Città del Vaticano; prompt on the Holy See]
swap.clue: A meeting in this city declared that doctrines issued ex cathedra are infallible, and was prompted by the Syllabus of Errors of Pius IX.

question.text: An Armenian ruler with this name known as the "Illuminator" was responsible for converting the Armeniansfrom Zoroastrianism to Christianity. The first pope with this name names a series of "chants" while the thirteenthnames a calendar which replaced the Julian.
question.clue: Henry IV walked to Canossa in a hair shirt to have an excommunication that was given to him by a pope of this name rescinded during the Investiture Controversy.

swap.leadin: During the Western Schism, competing popes ruled from Rome and this city starting in 1378.
swap.text: Name this French city where seven popes resided during the "Babylonian Captivity."
swap.clue: This city was called "a sewer where all the muck of the universe collects" by Petrarch, who coined an enduring Biblical nickname for it.

question.leadin: This council was preceded by a failed attempt at Pisa.
question.text: Name this church council that ended the Western Schism and burned Jan Hus burned at the stake for promoting Utraquism. Much to the ire of Martin V and other popes, it declared that future councils should meet every 10 years.
question.clue: It was here that Pope Gregory XII helped elect Oddone Colonna as his own replacement.

swap.leadin: God wills this bonus! answer some of the following about the event in which other people used that motto.
swap.text: The phrase Deus vult, or God Wills It, was used during by Pope Urban II during this council, which also led to the excommunication of Philip I of France. This council began a conflict led by Peter the Hermit against the Seljuk Turks.
swap.clue: Due to an adulterous relationship with Bertrade de Montfort, Countess of Anjou, Philip I was excommunicated at this church council, which was preceded by the council of Placentia.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the history of Malta.
question.text: This Christian military order ruled Malta for over two and a half centuries, until Ferdinand von Hompesch zu Bolheim surrendered it to Napoleon in 1798.
question.answerHtml: Knights Hospitaller [or Knights of Saint John, accept Order in place of “Knights” in either]
question.clue: This group was founded by merchants from Amalfi, and was later led by Gerard Thom.

swap.leadin: Members of this organization were accused of worshiping a cat by Phillip IV of France.
swap.text: Name this organization whose members were arrested and tortured on orders from Phillip IV. This organization was dissolved by Pope Clement V while led by Jacques de Molay.
swap.answerHtml: Knights Templar [or Poor Fellow-Soldiers of Christ and of the Temple of Solomon; prompt on Templars]
swap.clue: At the Battle of Montgisard, they helped defeat Saladin's army, and they were founded after the First Crusade by Hugues de Payens and Godfrey de Saint-Omer to protect pilgrims traveling to the Holy Land.

question.leadin: Identify the following about some popes named Clement.
question.text: Clement XIV abolished this religious order in 1773. This order was founded by Ignatius of Loyola and was a key force in the Counter-Reformation.
question.clue: Two members of this group prepared the translation of the Treaty of Nerchinsk and another created a lunisolar calendar for the last Ming emperor.

swap.leadin: It resulted in the election of the Swiss Antipope Clement VII.
swap.text: Identify this period in which Philip IV of France moved the Papacy to Avignon, named after a duration of time in the Old Testament.
swap.clue: This term which also applies to an exile of Jews from Judah begun by Nebuchadnezzar and ended by Cyrus the Great.

question.leadin: Terrorists planned to assassinate this pope during a visit to the Philippines in the first phase of the Bojinka Plot.
question.text: Name this pope who established World Youth Day in 1985. This pope's visit to his home country motivated the formation of the Solidarity movement, which went on to end communist rule in that country.
question.clue: This man made a prison visit to forgive Mehmet Ali Agca, a member of the Grey Wolves who tried to kill him.

swap.text: This dogma, that the pope cannot err when speaking in his official role as pontiff, was propounded at the First Vatican Council.
swap.clue: What is the two-word name in English for the idea that the pope speaks for the whole church and cannot be in error?

question.leadin: Answer some questions about the year 1968.
question.text: In July, this pope issued the encyclical Humanae vitae, which condemned artificial birth control. In 1968, this pope who closed the Second Vatican Council also beatified the Korean Martyrs.
question.answerHtml: Paul VI (or Giovanni Battista Enrico Antonio Maria Montini)
question.clue: This pope who canonized the Uganda martyrs and later visited Kampala in 1969 in the first papal trip to Africa. This pope presided over the end of Vatican II after the death of John XXIII ("the twenty-third").

swap.leadin: This pope initiated the "Babylonian Captivity" by moving the papal curia from Rome to Avignon.
swap.text: Name this pope, who withdrew the bull unam sanctam, which asserted papal supremacy over earthly rulers. This pope worked with Philip IV to eliminate the Knights Templar.
swap.clue: He rescinded an earlier papal bull which proclaimed that outside of the church, there is no salvation.

question.leadin: Identify the following ecumenical councils from their theological statements.
question.text: This unrecognized council of 1409 failed to end the Western Schism, and its decision was superseded by the later Council of Constance.
question.clue: Philargi was elected and took the name Alexander V, but the results were ignored since Urban VI and Clement VII both refused to recognize this council.

swap.leadin: This event was caused by the election of Pope Urban VI and the accusations of intimidation which led to his election.
swap.text: Name this event, during which there were two or three claimants to the Papacy, residing in Rome, France and, for a brief period, Pisa. This event is sometimes described as "great", causing confusion with a separate event of 1054.
swap.answerHtml: The Western Schism [accept Great Divide or Great Occidental Schism or Schism of 1378 or Great Western Schism, do not accept or prompt on “Great Schism” or “Schism”]
swap.clue: Pierre d'Ailly ("dah-YEE") and Jean Gerson ("zhawn zhair-SON") promoted a conciliar resolution to this conflict, which began when 13 rebels staged an election in Fondi ("FOHN-dee") with regalia stolen by a camerlengo.

question.text: Saint Catherine of Siena persuaded this pope to move the papacy back to Rome. This pope also hired John Hawkwood to fight on his behalf in the War of the Eight Saints.
question.answerHtml: Pope <u>Gregory XI</u> [or Pierre-Roger de <u>Beaufort</u>; prompt on “<u>Gregory</u>”]

swap.leadin: After the election of Pope Clement V, Philip IV of France forced him to remain in that country, where his successor, Pope John XXIII built a Lavish palace in a city on the Rhone where he moved the Papal court,FTPE.
swap.text: Name this city in which 7 popes resided during its namesake papacy and in which a second line of illegitimate popes reigned during the Great Western Schism.
swap.clue: The man who ended this time period did so after reading a letter written by Catherine of Siena.

question.text: In 1644, this pope born Maffeo Barberini died. He was a friend of Galileo and it was he to whom Galileo retorted, "But it does move."
question.clue: Unlike his successor Innocent X, this pope followed a relatively pro-French policy which was concerned with maintaining neutrality during the Thirty Years' War.

swap.text: Carafa's nephew Gian Petro, who forced Rome's Jews to live in a ghetto, was the fourth Pope of this name. The Tridentine Catechism was established at a Council inaugurated by the third Pope of this name.
swap.clue: Another member of this family was the final Republican opponent of extending the PATRIOT Act after filling defeating John Conway and Trey Grayson to fill Jim Bunning's Senate seat.
